speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to begin our evaluation, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and did they start suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your significant weight loss, chronic alcohol use, and steroid history alongside progressive arm weakness, could you describe exactly where you feel the sensation loss and whether you have noticed any numbness in your neck or hand?

REQUEST TEST: CBC, CMP, TSH, HbA1c, Vitamin B12, and Magnesium.
REQUEST IMAGES: Right arm MRI with contrast.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The patient's description of burning pain, weakness, and sensory loss in the right arm, combined with weight loss and significant risk factors for malignancy (smoking, alcohol, steroid use), is highly concerning for an underlying tumor compressing a nerve root or brachial plexus. Given the urgency, please describe if you have noticed any visible muscle wasting, weakness in your hand grip compared to the left side, or pain radiating from your neck.

REQUEST TEST: Chest CT, Brain MRI, and EMG/Nerve Conduction Study.
REQUEST IMAGES: Right Arm MRI with contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital_Signs: Temperature 99.5°F (37.5°C), Blood_Pressure 177/108 mmHg, Heart_Rate 90/min, Respiratory_Rate 17/min, Oxygen_Saturation 98% on room air; Neurological_Examination: Strength_Assessment 2/5 strength in the right arm and 5/5 strength in the left arm, Sensory_Examination Decreased sensation in the right arm, Reflexes Normal, Coordination Unaffected; tests: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC Within normal limits, Hemoglobin Within normal limits, Platelets Within normal limits, Chest_X-ray: Findings Mass noted at the apex of the right lung, CT_Chest: Findings Solid mass at the apex of the right lung, suggestive of a tumor.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor).

The CT and X-ray findings of a solid mass at the right lung apex, combined with your progressive right arm weakness, sensory loss, and burning pain, are classic for a tumor compressing the lower cervical nerve roots or brachial plexus. Given your age, smoking history, and significant weight loss, this is highly suspicious for primary lung malignancy, likely non-small cell lung cancer. I recommend immediate referral for a biopsy of the lung mass and further staging with a PET scan.
